glosses: to prune (trim a tree or shrub)
Ébrancher jusqu’à une certaine hauteur ou éclaircir en coupant une partie des branches.

examples.text: Il faut avoir soin de les élaguer convenablement et de détruire le gui parasite qui les envahit fréquemment.
Ainsi, l’on est plus riche, plus on est dépourvu : car l’esprit crée ce qui lui manque : l’arbre touffu que l’on élague monte plus haut. Moins j’ai et plus je suis…
Ensuite, il est impératif de n’élaguer que les branches mortes […]
Voici venu le moment d’élaguer.

glosses: Retrancher dans un ouvrage de l’esprit ce qui l’allonge inutilement et nuit à sa force, à son éclat.

examples.text: Cet exorde a besoin d’être élagué.
Il faudrait élaguer cette scène.
Élaguer un discours, un poème.
Il y a beaucoup à élaguer dans ce développement.

glosses: Supprimer les éléments inutiles.

examples.text: Elle finit d’ailleurs par trouver sa vie heureuse, après en avoir élagué les soucis matériels, car elle allait dîner tous les jours en ville, après avoir travaillé depuis le lever du soleil.

glosses: A plum.
The dried, wrinkled fruit of certain species of plum.
Something wrinkly like a prune.

examples.text: We are not free when we are in the grip of the false conditioning that decrees that we need sex. We are not free if we believe the culture's ominous warnings that we will become "horny" (what a callous, offensive word) and frustrated and neurotic and finally shrivel up into prunes and have to abandon hope of being good, creative, effective people.

glosses: An old woman, especially a wrinkly one.
To become wrinkled like a dried plum, as the fingers and toes do when kept submerged in water.

examples.text: I hardly left that spot in my pool that month even when my fingers pruned and chlorine dried out my skin.

glosses: To remove excess material from a tree or shrub; to trim, especially to make more healthy or productive.

examples.text: A good grape grower will prune the vines once a year.
But poore old man, thou prun'ſt a rotten tree, / That cannot ſo much as a bloſſome yeelde
Our delightful task / To prune these growing plants, and tend these flowers.

glosses: To cut down or shorten (by the removal of unnecessary material).

examples.text: to prune a budget, or an essay
taking into consideration how they [laws] are to be pruned and reformed

glosses: To remove (something unnecessary) for the sake of cutting down or shortening that which it was previously part of.

examples.text: When internal dissension and a decline in popularity set in, Johnny was pruned from the Crests.

glosses: To remove unnecessary branches from a tree data structure.

To preen; to prepare; to dress.

examples.text:

Prowdly to prune, and sett on every side.
